questions.question:
'When it is raining, peacocks dance.'

Based only on this sentence, which one of the following options is necessarily true?

options.A: Peacocks dance only when it is raining.
options.B: When peacocks dance, it is raining.
options.C: When peacocks are not dancing, it is not raining.
options.D: When it is not raining, peacocks do not dance.

questions.explanation:
The statement is [latex]\text{Raining}\Rightarrow\text{Dancing}[/latex]. The only thing logically guaranteed to also be true is its contrapositive: [latex]\neg\text{Dancing}\Rightarrow\neg\text{Raining}[/latex], i.e. "When peacocks are not dancing, it is not raining." A contrapositive is always logically equivalent to the original conditional, so it must hold whenever the original does.

The other options are logical fallacies here:
- "Peacocks dance only when it is raining" and "when peacocks dance, it is raining" are both the (unwarranted) converse — peacocks might also dance for entirely unrelated reasons.
- "When it is not raining, peacocks do not dance" is the (unwarranted) inverse — again, nothing rules out peacocks dancing on a dry day for some other reason.

Answer: When peacocks are not dancing, it is not raining.

questions.question:
Consider the relationships among P, Q, R, S, and T:

P is the brother of Q.
S is the daughter of Q.
T is the sister of S.
R is the mother of Q.

The following statements are made based on the relationships given above.

R is the grandmother of S.
P is the uncle of S and T.
R has only one son.
Q has only one daughter.

Which one of the following options is correct?
questions.explanation:
From the given facts: [latex]P[/latex] is [latex]Q[/latex]'s brother; [latex]S[/latex] is [latex]Q[/latex]'s daughter; [latex]T[/latex] is [latex]S[/latex]'s sister (so [latex]T[/latex] is also [latex]Q[/latex]'s daughter); [latex]R[/latex] is [latex]Q[/latex]'s mother.

- "R is the grandmother of S": since [latex]R[/latex] is [latex]Q[/latex]'s mother and [latex]S[/latex] is [latex]Q[/latex]'s daughter, [latex]R[/latex] is indeed [latex]S[/latex]'s grandmother. True.
- "P is the uncle of S and T": [latex]P[/latex], as [latex]Q[/latex]'s sibling, is uncle to [latex]Q[/latex]'s children [latex]S[/latex] and [latex]T[/latex]. True.
- "R has only one son": we're only told [latex]P[/latex] is a brother of [latex]Q[/latex] — nothing rules out [latex]R[/latex] having other sons not mentioned. Not established, so not necessarily true.
- "Q has only one daughter": we're explicitly told about two daughters of [latex]Q[/latex] ([latex]S[/latex] and her sister [latex]T[/latex]), directly contradicting this. False.

Answer: Both (1) and (2) are true.

questions.question: An unbiased six-faced dice whose faces are marked with numbers [latex]1,2,3,4,5[/latex], and [latex]6[/latex] is rolled twice in succession and the number on the top face is recorded each time. The probability that the number appearing in the second roll is an integer multiple of the number appearing in the first roll is ________
questions.explanation:
For the first roll [latex]=a[/latex] and second roll [latex]=b[/latex] (each uniformly from [latex]\{1,\ldots,6\}[/latex]), we need [latex]b[/latex] to be a multiple of [latex]a[/latex]. Count, for each value of [latex]a[/latex], how many values of [latex]b\in\{1,\ldots,6\}[/latex] are multiples of [latex]a[/latex]:

[latex]\begin{array}{c|c}a&\text{multiples of }a\text{ in }\{1,...,6\}\\\hline1&1,2,3,4,5,6\ (6)\\2&2,4,6\ (3)\\3&3,6\ (2)\\4&4\ (1)\\5&5\ (1)\\6&6\ (1)\end{array}[/latex]

Total favorable outcomes [latex]=6+3+2+1+1+1=14[/latex] out of [latex]6\times6=36[/latex] equally likely outcomes.

Probability [latex]=\dfrac{14}{36}=\dfrac{7}{18}[/latex].

Answer: 7/18

questions.question:
Based only on the conversation below, identify the logically correct inference:

"Even if I had known that you were in the hospital, I would not have gone there to see you", Ramya told Josephine.

options.A: Ramya knew that Josephine was in the hospital.
options.B: Ramya did not know that Josephine was in the hospital.
options.C: Ramya and Josephine were once close friends; but now, they are not.
options.D: Josephine was in the hospital due to an injury to her leg.

questions.explanation:
The sentence "Even if I had known that you were in the hospital, I would not have gone there to see you" is a counterfactual conditional — the phrase "even if I had known" (past perfect, hypothetical) directly implies that Ramya did not, in fact, know that Josephine was in the hospital at the time. The sentence only tells us what Ramya claims she would have done in that hypothetical scenario, not anything about their friendship history or the reason Josephine was hospitalized.

Answer: Ramya did not know that Josephine was in the hospital.

Hari(H), Gita(G), Irfan(I) and Saira(S) are siblings (i.e., brothers and sisters). All were born on 1st January. The age difference between any two successive siblings (that is born one after another) is less than three years. Given the following facts:

i. Hari's age + Gita's age > Irfan's age + Saira's age
ii. The age difference between Gita and Saira is one year. However Gita is not the oldest and Saira is not the youngest.
iii. There are no twins.

In what order they were born (oldest first)?
questions.explanation:
G and S differ by 1 year, so they are adjacent. G is not oldest and S not youngest.

- HSIG: G and S are not adjacent [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] fails (ii)
- IGSH: I older than G and S older than H, so I + S [latex]\gt[/latex] G + H [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] fails (i)
- IHSG: I older than H and S older than G, so I + S [latex]\gt[/latex] H + G [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] fails (i)
- SGHI: S, G oldest pair; H + G [latex]\gt[/latex] I + S is possible (e.g. ages 10, 9, 7, 5: 16 [latex]\gt[/latex] 15)

Answer: SGHI

questions.question:
In the [latex]2020[/latex] summer Olympics' Javelin throw finals, Neeraj Chopra exhibited a spectacular performance to win the gold medal. The silver medal was won by Jakub Vadlejch and the bronze medal was won by Vitezlav Vesely. There were six rounds of throws with each athlete having one throw per round. The best of all the throws of each athlete is considered for the medal. Following were the observations about the throws:

i.) The first and second rounds were dominated by Neeraj Chopra with a gold medal performance in his second throw, while the other two athletes did not have any medal winning throws in these rounds.

ii.) The throws in the last round by both Jakub Vadlejch and Vitezlav Vesely were fouls and were not considered for scoring.

iii.) After four rounds, Vitezlav Vesely was in the second position and could not improve upon his best throw in the succeeding rounds.

iv.) In the fourth round, the throw by Jakub Vadlejch was the best in that round.

In which round did Vitezlav Vesely have his best throw?
questions.explanation:
Work through the clues step by step:

(i) Rounds [latex]1[/latex] and [latex]2[/latex] belong entirely to Neeraj Chopra (his 2nd throw was gold-medal-worthy); Jakub and Vesely achieved none of their medal-relevant (best) throws in these two rounds. So neither Jakub's nor Vesely's personal-best throw happened in round 1 or 2 — both of their best throws must fall somewhere in rounds [latex]3[/latex]-[latex]6[/latex].

(ii) Both Jakub's and Vesely's round-[latex]6[/latex] throws were fouls (not counted at all), so neither of their best throws can be in round [latex]6[/latex] either. This narrows their best throws down to rounds [latex]3,4,5[/latex].

(iii) After [latex]4[/latex] rounds, Vesely already held [latex]2[/latex]nd position, and he never improved on this best throw afterward (rounds [latex]5[/latex] and [latex]6[/latex] didn't help him). So Vesely's personal-best throw must have occurred within rounds [latex]1[/latex]-[latex]4[/latex] — combined with the earlier elimination of rounds [latex]1,2[/latex], this leaves only round [latex]3[/latex] or round [latex]4[/latex] as candidates.

(iv) In round [latex]4[/latex], it was Jakub's throw that was the best of that round (not Vesely's) — this is consistent with Vesely's personal best having already been set earlier, in round [latex]3[/latex], and round [latex]4[/latex] simply being a round where Jakub (not Vesely) peaked.

Putting it together, Vesely's best throw was in round 3.

Answer: Third

questions.question:
In the diagram, the lines QR and ST are parallel to each other. The shortest distance between these two lines is half the shortest distance between the point P and line QR. What is the ratio of the area of the triangle PST to the area of the trapezium SQRT?
Note: The figure shown is representative.
questions.explanation:
Let [latex]h[/latex] be the perpendicular distance from [latex]P[/latex] to line [latex]QR[/latex] (the full height of triangle [latex]PQR[/latex]). We're told the distance between the parallel lines [latex]ST[/latex] and [latex]QR[/latex] is [latex]h/2[/latex], which means [latex]ST[/latex] sits exactly halfway between [latex]P[/latex] and [latex]QR[/latex] (height from [latex]P[/latex] down to [latex]ST[/latex] is also [latex]h/2[/latex], since [latex]h/2+h/2=h[/latex]).

Since [latex]ST\parallel QR[/latex] and [latex]ST[/latex] is at exactly half the height from [latex]P[/latex], triangle [latex]PST[/latex] is similar to triangle [latex]PQR[/latex] with linear scale factor [latex]\tfrac12[/latex], so its area is [latex]\left(\tfrac12\right)^2=\tfrac14[/latex] of triangle [latex]PQR[/latex]'s area.

Area of trapezium [latex]SQRT[/latex] [latex]=[/latex] Area([latex]PQR[/latex]) [latex]-[/latex] Area([latex]PST[/latex]) [latex]=1-\tfrac14=\tfrac34[/latex] of Area([latex]PQR[/latex]).

Ratio [latex]=\dfrac{\text{Area}(PST)}{\text{Area}(SQRT)}=\dfrac{1/4}{3/4}=\dfrac13[/latex]

Answer: 1/3

questions.question:
The corners and mid-points of the sides of a triangle are named using the distinct letters P, Q, R, S, T and U, but not necessarily in the same order. Consider the following statements:

The line joining P and R is parallel to the line joining Q and S.
P is placed on the side opposite to the corner T.
S and U cannot be placed on the same side.

Which one of the following statements is correct based on the above information?

options.A: P cannot be placed at a corner
options.B: S cannot be placed at a corner
options.C: U cannot be placed at a mid-point
options.D: R cannot be placed at a corner

questions.explanation:
In a triangle, two such lines can be parallel only if one joins two midpoints and the other lies along the opposite side.

- If Q and S are the two midpoints, S is a midpoint.
- Otherwise P and R are the midpoints, and Q, S lie on the parallel side (its two corners and its midpoint). P sits on the side opposite T, so T is also a point of that side, and U is the remaining corner. S cannot share a side with U, and both corners of that side share a side with U. So S must be the midpoint.

In every case S is a midpoint.

Answer: S cannot be placed at a corner
